title: Formal letters and emails
subtitle: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing in response to, Yours faithfully
summary: Use the fixed phrases that open, fill and close a formal letter or email in English.

lesson.heading: A model formal letter
lesson.text: Here is a short letter answering a job advertisement. Every sentence in it is a phrase you can reuse.

examples.text: **I am writing in response to** your advertisement about job opportunities for **graduates**.
examples.note: in response to = in reply to; graduates = people with a university degree

examples.text: **I would be grateful if you could** send me **further details** of the training schemes.
examples.note: slightly more formal than Please could you ...; further details = more information

examples.text: I am **available** for interview at any time.
**I look forward to hearing from you.**

lesson.heading: How to begin and end
rows: You do not know the name
Dear Mr Wilkinson / Dear Ms Drew
lesson.note: At the end of a formal letter you **sign** your name (your **signature**) and then print it underneath.

lesson.heading: Good news and bad news
lesson.text: **I regret to inform you** is the formal way to say *I am sorry to say*; **I am pleased to inform you** is the formal way to say *I am happy to say*. An **application** is an official request for something.

examples.text: **I regret to inform you** that your **application** has not been successful.
**I am pleased to inform you** that your application has been successful.
Thank you for your letter **regarding** the damage to your vehicle.

lesson.heading: Asking and confirming
lesson.text: Use **enquire about** to ask about something, and **confirm in writing** to say in a letter that something is certain.

examples.text: I am writing to **enquire about** English courses at your school.
You will need to **confirm** the booking **in writing**.

lesson.heading: Thanking, apologising and enclosing
lesson.text: To say sorry, use **apologise for** or **Please accept our apologies for**. A **delay** is when something arrives later than expected. If you put something in the same envelope, you **enclose** it.

examples.text: We would like to thank you for offering your **support**.
We would like to **apologise for** the delay.
**Please accept our apologies for** the delay.

examples.note: = I am sending it with this letter

lesson.heading: Informal into formal
rows: Thank you for your letter regarding ...
I am pleased to inform you ...
I would like to enquire about ...
I would be grateful if you could send me the details.
I'm sending a copy of my CV.
I enclose a copy of my CV.

lesson.text: Yours faithfully goes with Dear Sir or Madam; Yours sincerely goes with a name. Remember: no name - faithfully; name - sincerely.

exercises.prompt: You do not know the person's name, so you start: '___,'
exercises.explanation: Dear Sir or Madam is used when you do not know the name.

exercises.prompt: You want more information, so you ask for further ___.
exercises.explanation: Further details = more information about something.

exercises.prompt: You expect a reply, so you close: 'I look forward ___.'
exercises.explanation: Look forward to + -ing: I look forward to hearing from you.

exercises.prompt: You do not know the person's name, so you end: 'Yours ___,'
exercises.explanation: Dear Sir or Madam goes with Yours faithfully.

exercises.prompt: You know the person's name, so you end: 'Yours ___,'
exercises.explanation: When you know the name, end with Yours sincerely.

exercises.prompt: Another way of ending a letter is 'Kind ___,'
exercises.explanation: Kind regards is a slightly less formal ending.

exercises.prompt: Match the everyday sentence with its formal version.

pairs.right: I am pleased to inform you ...

pairs.left: I want to ask about the course.
pairs.right: I would like to enquire about the course.

pairs.left: I'm sending a copy of my CV.
pairs.right: I enclose a copy of my CV.

exercises.prompt: Make it formal: 'We want to say sorry for the delay.' -> 'Please accept ___ for the delay.'
exercises.explanation: Please accept our apologies for ... is the formal way to say sorry.

exercises.prompt: Make it formal: 'Please send me the details.' -> 'I would be ___ send me the details.'
exercises.explanation: I would be grateful if you could ... is a polite formal request.

exercises.prompt: Make it formal: 'Could you say that's definite in a letter?' -> 'Could you ___ that in writing?'
exercises.explanation: Confirm something in writing = write to say it is certain.

exercises.prompt: Letter: 'I am writing in ___ to your letter of 10 February.'
exercises.explanation: In response to / in reply to your letter.

exercises.prompt: Letter: 'We ___ to inform you that there are delays of up to four weeks on most orders.'
exercises.explanation: We regret to inform you introduces bad news.

exercises.prompt: Which ending matches 'Dear Sir or Madam'?
exercises.explanation: No name at the top means Yours faithfully at the bottom.

exercises.statement: I look forward to hear from you.
exercises.explanation: I look forward to hearing from you. Look forward to is followed by the -ing form.
